name: The Okura Tokyo
insider_take: This legendary Tokyo icon has been the epitome of understated Japanese luxury since 1962, hosting world leaders and celebrities in its uniquely serene atmosphere.
whats_special: The Okura's original main building was a masterpiece of 1960s Japanese modernist architecture, featuring the famous hexagonal lobby lanterns and stunning views of the Imperial Palace gardens. The hotel pioneered the concept of "Japanese hospitality with international standards" and remains famous for its impeccable service and the world-renowned Okura butter rolls served at breakfast.
pro_tip: Book a room facing the Imperial Palace for sunrise views over the East Gardens, and don't miss afternoon tea in the lobby - it's where Tokyo's elite have gathered for decades.
dont_miss: The hotel's proximity to the Imperial Palace East Gardens (2-minute walk), the traditional Yamazato restaurant with its kaiseki cuisine, and the fact that you're staying in the same spot where The Beatles stayed during their 1966 Japan tour - their suite is now part of hotel lore.
pros: Iconic Japanese hospitality with legendary omotenashi service
Timeless elegant design blending traditional and modern aesthetics
Prime location in Toranomon with easy access to Imperial Palace
Exceptional dining including renowned Japanese and French cuisine
cons: Classic understated style may feel conservative to some guests
